image_metadata.File:HAtomOrbitals.png:
First few [hydrogen atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/hydrogen_atom) orbitals; cross section showing color-coded probability density for different n=1,2,3 and l="s","p","d"; note: m=0
The picture shows the first few hydrogen atom orbitals \(energy eigenfunctions\). These are cross-sections of the probability density that are color-coded \(black=zero density, white=highest density\). The [angular momentum quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azimuthal_quantum_number) l is denoted in each column, using the usual [spectroscopic letter code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spectroscopic_notation) \("s" means l=0; "p": l=1; "d": l=2\). The [prinipal quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_quantum_number) n \(=1,2,3,...\) is marked to the right of each row. For all pictures the [magnetic quantum number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_quantum_number) m has been set to 0, and the cross-sectional plane is the x-z plane \(z is the vertical axis\). The probability density in three-dimensional space is obtained by rotating the one shown here around the z-axis.

Note the striking similarity of this picture to the diagrams of the normal modes of displacement of a soap film membrane oscillating on a disk bound by a wire frame. See, e.g., _Vibrations and Waves_, A.P. French, M.I.T. Introductory Physics Series, 1971, [ISBN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISBN) [0393099369](//commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:BookSources/0393099369), page 186, Fig. 6-13. See also [Normal vibration modes of a circular membrane](http://web.mat.bham.ac.uk/C.J.Sangwin/Teaching/CircWaves/waves.html).
image_metadata.File:Hydrogen eigenstate n4 l3 m1.png:
Calculated 4f<sub>1</sub> [orbital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_orbital) of an electron's eigenstate in the Coulomb-field of a hydrogen nucleus. An [eigenstate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eigenfunction) is a state which keeps it's shape except for a complex phase when the [Hamilton operator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamiltonian_(quantum_mechanics)) is applied, thus being invariant in time while obeying the [Schrödinger equation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schr%C3%B6dinger_equation). The orbital is aligned around the z-axis, but remains an eigenfunction if rotated to any direction.

The [wavefunction](#wavefunction) is:

ψ4,3,1(r,ϑ,φ)=(12a0)318⋅7!⋅e−r/(4a0)⋅(1r2a0)3⋅Y31(ϑ,φ)


The state is an eigenstate of [H](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamiltonian_(quantum_mechanics)), [L](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_momentum_operator)² and [L](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angular_momentum_operator)<sub>z</sub>, which constitute a [complete set of commuting observables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/complete_set_of_commuting_observables). The [quantum numbers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/quantum_number) mean that the following quantities have a sharp certain value:



- n = 4: [Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_quantum_number): E=−1Ry/n2=−13.6eV/16
- l = 3: [Angular momentum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Azimuthal_quantum_number): |L|=l(l+1)ℏ=23ℏ
- m = 1: [Angular momentum in z-direction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_quantum_number): Lz=mℏ=ℏ



Since l=3, this is called a f-orbital. The depicted rigid body is where the probability density exceeds a certain value. The color shows the complex phase of the wavefunction, where blue means real positive, red means imaginary positive, yellow means real negative and green means imaginary negative. The image is [raytraced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_tracing_(graphics)) using modified [Phong lighting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phong_reflection_model).

The [fine structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/fine_structure) is neglected.
